title: Curtailments on Aged Inventory under the Kestrel Dealer Wholesale Floorplan Line
content:
**Rule.** A new unit owes the grade's new-unit curtailment percent of its original advance once its floor days reach the grade's new-unit curtailment start and again every new-unit curtailment interval; a used unit owes the grade's used-unit curtailment percent from the used-unit curtailment start and every used-unit curtailment interval, and must be paid in full by the grade's used-unit maximum floor days. Demonstrators curtail the demonstrator curtailment percent each month.

A curtailment under the Kestrel Dealer Wholesale Floorplan Line is a scheduled principal payment on an aged floored unit. Each one is recorded against the unit's VIN with its sequence number, and it reduces the line's outstanding wholesale principal. The day counts, percents and intervals are those of the line's Kestrel Wholesale Risk Grade.

## Questions the rule answers

**How is a unit's age on the floor measured?**
By its floor days: the calendar days the unit has been floored, counted from the unit's advance date to today.

**When does a new unit owe its first curtailment?**
Once its floor days reach the grade's new-unit curtailment start. A count that equals the start figure has reached it; a count one day short has not.

**When are later new-unit curtailments owed?**
Again every new-unit curtailment interval after the first, each interval measured in days of floor time.

**What is each curtailment figured on?**
On the unit's original advance. The percent is applied to the amount first advanced on the unit, so every curtailment on one unit is the same amount.

**How does a used unit differ?**
A used unit follows its own start, percent and interval, and in addition must be paid in full by the grade's used-unit maximum floor days.

**What do demonstrators owe?**
A demonstrator curtails the demonstrator curtailment percent of its original advance each month.

## Worked schedule (hypothetical)

Hypothetical terms invented for this illustration and belonging to no Kestrel Wholesale Risk Grade: a new-unit start of 150 days, an interval of 45 days and a curtailment percent of 10; a new unit advanced at 30000 USD.

| Floor days | Start or interval reached | Curtailment owed |
|---|---|---|
| 149 | No | None yet |
| 150 | First curtailment | 10 percent of 30000 USD, which is 3000 USD |
| 195 | Second curtailment, 45 days after the first | 3000 USD |
| 240 | Third curtailment | 3000 USD |
